A condensed sharp serif for the title, a warm grotesk with ink traps for captions; both narrow, both restrained.
Hairline contrast at opsz 96 against a condensed industrial sans (wdth 85): glamour over machinery.
Garamond-born display capitals with small caps for labels; Archivo semi-condensed keeps captions modern and legible.
News serif headlines (opsz 72), Plex Sans for names and Plex Mono for dates and data: a newspaper's hierarchy.
A round heavy serif title and the narrator's own marker hand for captions (INFM 40, BNCE seeded per glyph).
A heavy-contrast serif title over a quiet news serif with optical sizes: a book jacket.
A blackletter gothic for the title, a fragile garalde for the lines: old print, a cold room.
Ritual flared capitals (Velvetyne) over a warm Goudy text with small caps.
A woodcut display for the card names, a news serif with optical sizes for the reading.
Redaction's eroded grades give real ink loss; Space Mono labels read like a stamp. Swap grades over time for decay.
A worn typewriter for dossiers and dates, a news serif for the narration cards.
A quiet condensed serif for memory, a retro mono for the timestamp: a home video label.
Inline tube capitals glow; a geometric grotesk and a code mono keep the information clean.
XROT/YROT turn the letters in 3D on the beat; a width-variable mono answers below.
Syne widens as it gains weight, so the title can open like a horizon; Plex Mono carries coordinates.
A condensed precise sans for titles (wdth 75), a quiet serif for the lines: generous space, one accent.
A tight neo-grotesk headline, a product-UI sans for claims, tabular figures for prices.
Bricolage at opsz 96 and wdth 75 shows its quirks in the headline; Geist keeps the UI and CTA sober.
A tall condensed didone (opsz high) against a geometric grotesk: a magazine cover.
A sharp serif with real small caps and tabular figures for prices; a grotesk with stylistic sets for claims.
Condensed scoreboard capitals (opsz 72) with tabular figures, a geometric grotesk for the rest.
A lettering-like italic display with a bouncing marker text face: Saturday-morning energy.
Pixel titles over a crisp variable mono; set the pixel face on whole pixels.
A soft wonky serif for the dish, a hand-drawn marker (Shantell Sans) for the notes in the margin.
Tall cut display caps for the place, a neutral sans for distances and names.
The YEAR axis melts the headline as the data moves; Plex carries the numbers.
Recursive alone: Sans Linear for headlines, Mono Casual for code; animate MONO or CASL as the software comes alive.
Geist for interface and copy, JetBrains Mono for code: the product speaks for itself.
Ojuju's ink cuts give a hand-cut title card; Familjen keeps subtitles friendly.
Fake-3D rotating display letters over a wide rounded sans: loud pop packaging.
A mischievous swash display over Garamond-born capitals.
Abstract 1971 geometric letters for the title, a width-variable mono for all text.
Collletttivo's eccentric grotesk with Velvetyne's ink-trap mono: a risograph zine.
Condensed League Gothic caps for the place, a Goudy Oldstyle text: two League classics.
A condensed Didone at opsz 100 for the title, a sober sans for labels.
An ultra-bold slab over a geometric gothic: a fairground poster.
A calm text serif for the claim, a precise sans for the CTA and legal line.
Archivo Expanded Black carries the line; one Caveat Brush word adds the hand; a JetBrains Mono label stays small.
Unbounded Black, wide and round, with one graffiti word from Sedgwick Ave Display; Space Mono for the tiny label.
Anton condensed caps and one Yellowtail sign-painter word: contrast of structure and slope only.
Big Shoulders Display Black, civic and industrial, with a personal Marck Script note; Plex Mono for dates.
Bricolage ExtraBold at wdth 75 with an Instrument Serif Italic word: structure + slope, an editorial cover.
Anybody at wdth 150 Black fills the frame; one Kalam Bold word is the friendly aside.
Dela Gothic One, very heavy, with a Mynerve notebook word; Figtree for any subtitles.
Syne ExtraBold (wide) with a fine Square Peg word; subtitles in Figtree (Inter only as the user's own choice).
